newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: DEFENCE FORCE RESTRUCTURING REVEALED TODAY
The Federal Government will today unveil its plan for a dramatic restructuring of the defence forces.
The Defence Minister, Ian McLachlan will launch what's called the "Defence Reform Program" based on an efficiency review.
Mr McLachlan says the 10-billion-dollar defence budget -- the one area quarantined from budget cuts -- must move more resources to the fighting front.
The Opposition predicts the review will mean job cuts worth 800-million dollars and the sell-off of defence land worth up to one-billion dollars.
The chiefs of the Army, Navy and Air Force met the Prime Minister last Friday to plead for more time to cope with the major changes in the review.
MAL COLSTON ADMITTED TO A BRISBANE HOSPITAL
Independent Federal MP Mal Colston has been admitted to a Brisbane hospital.
A spokeswoman for the Wesley Hospital says the Senator was admitted with a medical condition and is currently resting.
She says the hospital won't be releasing any further details of the Senators condition until this morning.
He is currently under investigation for allegedly rorting parliamentary travel expenses, and has been asked by the Prime Minster to step down from his position as deputy president of the Senate.
BANK OF MELBOURNE TAKEOVER INVESTIGATION TO GO FOR WEEKS
Head of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Allan Fels, says a decision on Westpac's planned takeover of Bank of Melbourne won't be made for some weeks.
The commission is investigating whether the takeover reduces competition in the banking market.

Speaking in Sydney last night, Professor Fels said that the removal of the "Six Pillars" policy - to allow the major banks and insurance companies to come together won't affect his view on the proposed merger.
ATSIC LEADER POSITIVE ON CENTURY ZINC GO AHEAD
ATSIC Deputy Chair, Ray Robinson, says he's positive the Century Zinc project will go ahead after negotiations with the four native title claimants yet to sign their support for the mine.
He says discussions with two of the claimants in Brisbane have been constructive.
Mr Robinson says he has given the group time to think about their position and they are going back to their community until Sunday.
He says he expects there will be a major announcment in Brisbane on Monday.
OLYMPIC STADIUM BUILDERS LIST ON STOCK EXCHANGE TODAY
The group which is building the Sydney Olympic Stadium is being listed on the Stock exchange today, but little trade is expected.
People who have bought the $10,000 gold packages from Stadium Australia will be able to trade their 30-year membership in the venue, and their shares.
However, they will not be able to sell their Olympic tickets.
Stadium Australia was more than 60 per cent undersubscribed in its float, and the underwriters have confirmed they won't be trading their 214 million share in the company at this stage.
HOMEFUND BORROWERS GET PETITION DECISION TODAY
Borrowers with the ill-fated Homefund housing loan scheme will find out today whether they can sue the New South Wales state government.

Six-hundred borrowers have petitioned the High Court to allow them to sue the government under trade practices law. The government successfully argued in the Federal Court that it wasn't bound by the law.
AUSTRALIA WINS ONE DAY SERIES
In cricket, Australia has clinched the one-day series against South Africa with an exciting victory in the sixth game of the seven-game series.
Chasing a victory target of 285, the Australians won by five wickets with one over to spare.
After South Africa made 7 for 284, Australia was in trouble at 3 for 58.
But a record fourth-wicket partnership of 189 between Steve Waugh and Michael Bevan put the Australians within sight of victory.
Bevan made 103 and Waugh 89.
The win gives Australia an unbeatable 4-2 lead in the best-of-seven series.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
